questions.question: [Test 76 - Q1] Dyslexia is a specific learning disorder that primarily manifests as difficulty in:
options: Reading, decoding words, and phonological processing
Performing basic arithmetic and algebraic calculations
Coordinating gross motor movements in outdoor sports
Expressing verbal emotions in social gatherings
questions.explanation: Dyslexia impairs a person's ability to read and comprehend text by affecting phonological awareness, spelling, and word recognition. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q2] Which assessment type is designed to evaluate student learning, acquisition, and academic achievement at the conclusion of an instructional period?
questions.explanation: Summative assessment is 'Assessment OF Learning', occurring at the end of a unit or term (e.g., final boards, term exams) to certify achievement. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q3] In Abraham Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, which level represents the ultimate realization of personal potential, self-fulfillment, and peak experiences?
questions.explanation: Self-actualization is the highest level of Maslow's pyramid, representing the drive to become everything that one is capable of becoming. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q4] Which educational theorist is credited with establishing 'Field Theory' in learning and pioneered Action Research in social psychology?
questions.explanation: Kurt Lewin introduced Field Theory, conceptualizing behavior as a function of the person and their psychological environment: B = f(P, E). (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q5] Jerome Bruner's concept of the 'Spiral Curriculum' advises that:
options: Complex ideas should be taught at a simplified level first, then revisited at increasing levels of difficulty
Students must study only in circular seating arrangements to improve social learning
Every topic must be completed within a single class session and never repeated
Science and mathematics must be completely separated from arts and languages
questions.explanation: A spiral curriculum revisits topics periodically with increasing depth and complexity, allowing learners to build upon their existing foundation. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q6] Noam Chomsky's theory of Language Acquisition proposes that children are born with an innate psychological mechanism known as the:
questions.explanation: Chomsky's LAD is a hypothetical biological module of the brain containing universal grammar rules that allows children to rapidly acquire any natural language. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q7] According to Robert Gagne's Conditions of Learning, how many hierarchical levels of learning are there, and what is the highest level?
questions.explanation: Gagne proposed 8 hierarchical levels of learning. The lowest is signal learning, and the highest, most complex level is problem-solving. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q8] The 'Project Method' of teaching, which focuses on solving real-world, purposeful problems in a social environment, was developed by:
questions.explanation: Kilpatrick formulated the Project Method based on pragmatism and the educational philosophies of his mentor, John Dewey. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q9] The 'Heuristic Method' of teaching, which places the student in the role of an active discoverer or researcher, was pioneered by:
questions.explanation: H. E. Armstrong developed the Heuristic Method (from the Greek 'heuriskein' meaning 'to discover') to foster scientific enquiry and self-learning. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q10] Who developed the linear model of 'Programmed Instruction', which breaks down learning material into small steps called 'frames' with immediate feedback?
questions.explanation: B. F. Skinner developed linear programmed instruction based on operant conditioning, whereas Norman Crowder developed branching programmed instruction. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q11] Which quantitative method, developed by Jacob L. Moreno, is used to measure and map social relations, attractions, and repulsions within a classroom or group?
questions.explanation: Sociometry is a tool used to visually map and analyze social structures, peer acceptance, and interpersonal relationships within a classroom. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q12] The classic formula for calculating the Intelligence Quotient (IQ), (Mental Age / Chronological Age) * 100, was first formulated by:
questions.explanation: William Stern of Germany first proposed the concept of IQ and its formula in 1912, which was subsequently adapted and popularized by Lewis Terman in the Stanford-Binet intelligence scale. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q13] According to National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, what is the new pedagogical and curricular structure replacing the existing 10+2 structure in Indian school education?
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 replaces the traditional 10+2 system with a 5+3+3+4 structure corresponding to Foundational (5 yrs), Preparatory (3 yrs), Middle (3 yrs), and Secondary (4 yrs) stages. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q14] Which of the following principles best characterizes Jean Piaget's theory of cognitive development regarding the process of Schema Adaptation?
questions.explanation: Piaget defined adaptation as the balance achieved through assimilation (incorporating new info into existing schemas) and accommodation (modifying existing schemas to fit new info). (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q15] In Lev Vygotsky's Socio-Cultural Theory, the term 'Scaffolding' refers to:
options: Temporary support given by a More Knowledgeable Other (MKO) during the learning process
Permanent structural changes in cognitive architecture
Rote memorization techniques for complex concepts
Standardized testing procedures in formative assessment
questions.explanation: Scaffolding is a supportive framework provided by a teacher or peer (MKO) within the Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) that is gradually removed as the learner gains independence. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q16] Under the Right to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act 2009, what is the mandatory Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) prescribed for primary schools (Classes I to V)?
questions.explanation: As per the RTE Act 2009, the Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) for primary schools (Classes 1-5) is mandated at 30:1 for enrollment up to 200 students. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q17] Formative Assessment is primarily aimed at which of the following instructional goals?
options: Providing ongoing feedback to improve learning and teaching during the instructional process
Assigning final grades at the end of an academic semester
Ranking students based on normative curve distribution
questions.explanation: Formative assessment is 'Assessment FOR Learning' designed to monitor student learning and provide continuous feedback to teachers and students to modify teaching-learning activities. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q18] In Bloom's Revised Taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl, 2001), which level represents the highest order of cognitive processing?
questions.explanation: In Anderson & Krathwohl's revised taxonomy (2001), 'Creating' (generating new ideas or products) replaced 'Evaluation' at the highest cognitive level. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q19] Which teaching model is based on Jerome Bruner's concept of Discovery Learning and Enactive-Iconic-Symbolic modes of representation?
questions.explanation: Bruner proposed constructivist discovery learning where learners build knowledge through enactive (action-based), iconic (image-based), and symbolic (language-based) modes. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q20] Inclusive Education in Indian classrooms fundamentally implies:
options: Educating children with special needs alongside non-disabled children in regular classrooms with appropriate adaptations
Establishing separate special schools for children with disabilities
Admitting only high-achieving gifted students in mainstream schools
Providing home-based schooling for all children with mild learning difficulties
questions.explanation: Inclusive education ensures that all children, regardless of their physical, cognitive, social, or linguistic abilities, learn together in the same mainstream educational environment. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).
